name: UFW World Title
epitaph: The federation's top championship, first won by Executioner on 19 November 1999 and changing hands seventeen more times over the nine months the fed ran. Layeth the Smack Down held it three times and Myst three times, the two of them trading it across January and again in the closing summer; Roody Poo, the fed's own house jobber, held it for two days in April after counting his own pinfall as the match's referee. Myst's third win, 20 August 2000, is the last reign it recorded.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW US Title
epitaph: A secondary singles championship, opened on Myst on 10 December 1999 and changing hands eighteen more times. Myst took it three times in its first five months and JD Stalker and The Total Package twice each. "The Scholar" Howard Porter's win of 20 August 2000 is the last change it recorded, and he is the belt's holder on the federation's own final Champions page.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW Tag Team Titles
epitaph: The federation's two-man championship, opened on CHAOS INC. on 24 December 1999. Fifteen reigns are recorded across fourteen teams, The Isolators, CHAOS INC., The Avator & Biohazard and Iceman & Myst each taking two. The Brainiacs' win of 18 August 2000 is the last it recorded, and they are the champions on the federation's own final Champions page.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW Cruiserweight Title
epitaph: A weight-class championship opened on Dream Master at the federation's first pay-per-view, 24 December 1999. Jaguar held it three times and Degenerate twice across a January-to-March run of short reigns. Professor Herbert D. Dorkiman's win of 20 August 2000 is the last change it recorded.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW Woman's Title
epitaph: A championship for the federation's women's division, opened on Mystic on 24 December 1999. Pandora and Fury traded it twice each through the spring. The federation recorded Thunder winning it on 28 May 2000 and, on the same date and as the belt's own final line, that the division was discontinued.

events.note: The federation's own Titleholder History page: the belt's final line reads "Division Discontinued", dated 28 May 2000.

source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW TV Title
epitaph: The federation's most-traded championship: twenty-three reigns in eight months, opened on The Body on 24 December 1999. Iceman held it three times and B.A. Bruiser three, Bloodshed, JiN and Anguish twice each. Nemesis' win of 22 August 2000 is the last title change of any kind the federation's own record records.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW Hardcore Title
epitaph: A no-rules championship opened on Slasher on 24 December 1999 and passed twenty more times, Raker taking it twice in the first two months. Hex's win of 20 August 2000 is the last change it recorded, and he is the belt's holder on the federation's own final Champions page.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW Rising Star Title
epitaph: A championship for the federation's newer members, opened on The Gimp on 26 March 2000 — four months into the run — and traded fifteen more times in five months, The Gimp and Havok each holding it twice. "The Scholar" Howard Porter's win of 19 July 2000 is the last change it recorded for it; the federation's own final Champions page bills him as holding this belt and the US Title at once.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html

name: UFW Stables Title
epitaph: A six-man championship contested between the federation's stables, opened on The Showtakers on 25 February 2000 and carried by The Legion, The Forsaken Brotherhood and The Congregation in turn. Two of its six recorded changes leave the holder undisclosed on the federation's own record, and the federation's own final Champions page lists the belt the same way.
source: UFW's own Titleholder History page, served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-title-history.html
